title: Felix and the Verdict
premise: Marguerite Pemberton, the reclusive archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years solving quietly what the police dismiss, hiding behind her records and a locked crypt. A nervous stranger pays her in advance to prove that his sister — the cathedral's beloved organist — has not yet been murdered, though everyone insists she died three years ago. Following paper trails through baptismal registers and forged death certificates, Marguerite discovers the 'dead' woman is alive, hidden as a witness to an inheritance fraud entangling the cathedral's own deanery. When the client turns up drowned in the crypt, Marguerite must abandon invisibility entirely: she finds the living witness, exposes the conspiracy at a public requiem, and finally accepts the ragtag circle of parish outsiders who have become her family.
about_author: Yara Kavanagh is a former parish secretary from the west of England who spent a decade cataloguing church archives before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who notice everything.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A trembling man named Elias Crane visits the archive after hours, paying triple her fee to prove his sister Vivian — supposedly dead three years — hasn't been murdered yet. Marguerite, wary of anything that threatens her anonymity, almost refuses. The emotional beat is reluctant curiosity: the money is real, and so is his terror.

chapters.title: Registers of the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She pulls burial records and finds Vivian Crane's death certificate — signed by the cathedral's own sub-dean, Father Ambrose Locke. But the handwriting on the register shifts mid-entry, a forgery signature she recognizes from a previous case. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt stirring a loneliness she keeps buried.

chapters.title: The Organist Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a brief interlude from Denzil, the homeless ex-organ tuner who sleeps in the crypt. They confirm no one has seen Vivian since her 'death,' yet someone plays the organ at midnight — music Vivian alone composed. Emotional beat: wonder edged with dread; the dead don't practice scales.

chapters.title: A Legacy in Trust
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Digging into probate files, she uncovers that Vivian was sole heir to a trust funding the cathedral's restoration — a trust now controlled by Father Locke and a solicitor named Harrow. If Vivian lives, the inheritance reverts. Emotional beat: cold clarity; motive found, danger confirmed.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Denzil's POV. Denzil witnesses strangers breaking into the locked crypt at night and tells Marguerite, who realizes the crypt isn't just sealed — it's being searched. She confronts Father Locke, who deflects with charm and a veiled threat about her own undocumented past. Emotional beat: fear for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Elias, Drowned
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Elias Crane is found floating in the crypt's cistern; police call it an accident, the fourth she's heard called by that word. Among his effects: a photograph of Vivian taken last month. Grief hardens into resolve — the murder he feared has happened, just not to whom he expected. Emotional beat: guilt and fury.

chapters.title: The Midnight Recital
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Denzil stake out the organ loft and catch the midnight player: a young woman, gaunt and frightened — Vivian herself, living in the triforium passages for three years, the sole witness to Harrow falsifying the founder's will. Emotional beat: relief colliding with terror as footsteps echo below them.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Hidden above the nave, Vivian recounts the night of the 'accident' she escaped and why she trusted no one — until Marguerite. Harrow's men are closing in; Marguerite must choose between spiriting Vivian away or standing publicly beside her. Emotional beat: two invisible women recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Requiem
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At Elias's memorial service, packed with the town, Marguerite engineers the climax: Vivian rises from the choir stalls, alive, while Marguerite presents the forged register and the true will to the assembled congregation and a detective who owes her three old favors. Locke collapses; Harrow flees into the crypt and is caught at the cistern where Elias died. Emotional beat: triumphant exposure.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue weeks later. The crypt is unsealed, the trust restored, and Vivian takes up the organ loft permanently. The chapter closes with Marguerite pinning a new shingle to the archive door — investigations accepted — surrounded by Denzil, Vivian, and the detective bearing cake. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen at last.
